map.A two-variable adventure in five chapter: An adventure about two variables in five chapters. It has six reader gates. Solve the math to move the story.
Bent patterns in the harvest dome. Reader: you're on the crew. Suit up.
map.Previously: beneath city hall, the crew: Last time: under city hall, the crew opened Ada's balance vault scale by scale and cleared the inequality fog. The city can breathe again. But out at the farm district, the great glass dome has started to drift...
map.The harvest dome feeds half of Axiom Cit: The harvest dome feeds half of Axiom City, and it's wilting. Idris, you and me. We lead this one together.
map.Co-op mode accepted. Look — the mist is: Team mode accepted. Look, the mist is so thick the crops can't even find the sun.
map.Wilting rows, runaway mist, temperature: Wilting rows, runaway mist, and the temperature drifting all night. Everyone grab a sensor.
Source of the bent patterns: the climate system. Something in there has causes and effects tangled.
map.Inside the dome. Fans the size of doors: Inside the dome. Fans as big as doors line the walls.
map.Test one. I run the fans; Owen reads the: Test one. I run the fans. Owen reads the thermometer. The longer the cooling fans run, the lower the dome temperature.
map.Name your players. The independent varia: Name your players. The independent variable is the one you change on purpose, the cause. The dependent variable answers it, the effect.
map.Two quantities, one relationship. Indepe: Two quantities, one relationship. Independent variable: the input you control. Dependent variable: the output that depends on it.
map.Game translation: independent is the but: Game words: independent is the button you press. Dependent is what happens on screen.
map.Your turn, reader. Tag the variables bef: Your turn, reader. Tag the variables before we touch another dial.
map.Scenario from Sora's test: \"The longer: Scenario from Sora's test: "The longer the cooling fans run, the lower the dome temperature." Tag both variables. Pick one answer in EACH group.
map.Conceptual: the independent variable is: Conceptual: the independent variable is the cause, the thing you set or control on purpose. The dependent variable is the effect. It responds. You can't set it directly.
map.Procedural: try the plant test first: yo: Procedural: try the plant test first. You choose how much water to give (you set it, so it is independent). The plant's growth answers (dependent). Now read the fan sentence the same way: which quantity gets SET, and which one REACTS?
map.VEX logged last night's temperature. A g: VEX logged last night's temperature. A graph is a picture of the relationship: time across the bottom, temperature up the side.
map.Reading order: left to right. Like a sen: Reading order: left to right. Like a sentence.
map.This line falls steadily, then levels of: This line falls steadily, then goes flat. Falling means cooling. Flat means holding.
map.A graph shows how the dependent variable: A graph shows how the dependent variable (up the side) changes as the independent variable (across the bottom) gets bigger.
map.Match the graph to its story, reader. Th: Match the graph to its story, reader. The dome is talking. Listen with your eyes.
map.VEX projects last night's log: the line: VEX shows last night's log: the line falls steadily, then levels off flat. Which story is this graph telling? Tap the matching card, then CHECK.
map.Conceptual: a graph reads like a sentenc: Conceptual: a graph reads like a sentence, left to right. Time passes as you move right. The height of the line is the temperature at that moment.
map.Procedural: split the line into its two: Procedural: split the line into its two pieces, in order. Piece one slants down. What is the temperature doing? Piece two runs level. What is it doing now? Find the story with those two parts in that order.
map.The irrigation deck. Pipes hum. A water: The irrigation deck. Pipes hum. A water meter blinks out numbers.
map.Water sensor data. A table puts the two: Water sensor data. A table puts the two variables side by side so the pattern can't hide.
map.Practice on a smaller machine first. A d: Practice on a smaller machine first. A drip line gave 1 hour → 3 liters, 2 → 6, 4 → 12. Its rule is the equation y = 3x: every y is 3 times its x. Note: the rule worked for EVERY row.
map.An equation is a rule for computing the: An equation is a rule for finding the dependent variable from the independent one. Test a rule on every row of the table. One lucky row proves nothing.
Now the main line. Hours in, liters out. Find its rule and we know how thirsty this dome really is.
Complete the table, then write the rule. Every row is a witness.
map.The main line's sensor log. Fill the mis: The main line's sensor log. Fill in the missing value, then choose the equation that matches every row.
map.Conceptual: the table hides one rule — e: Conceptual: the table hides one rule. Every y is made from its x the SAME way, in every row. A rule that fits only one row is luck, not a rule.
map.Procedural: compare each pair: 1 → 4, 2: Procedural: compare each pair: 1 → 4, 2 → 8, 3 → 12. Is y always the same MULTIPLE of its x? Find that number with row one, check it on rows two and three, then use it at x = 5.
map.Same data, third costume. Plot hours and: Same data, third costume. Plot hours and liters together and each pair becomes a point, a coordinate pair (x, y).
map.Order is law: (hours, liters). Across fi: Order is law: (hours, liters). Across first, then up. Flip them and you tell a different story.
map.The pump logged one reading before it cr: The pump logged one reading before it crashed: "after 5 hours, 20 liters." Somewhere on this grid is that exact moment.
map.A coordinate pair (x, y) marks one momen: A coordinate pair (x, y) marks one moment of a relationship: x = the independent value, y = the dependent value. Order matters.
map.Tap the point that says it, reader — and: Tap the point that says it, reader. Only that point.
map.The pump's last reading: \"after 5 hours: The pump's last reading: "after 5 hours, 20 liters." Four points are plotted. Tap the coordinate pair that means exactly that. Remember the order: (hours, liters).
map.Conceptual: an ordered pair reads (x, y): Conceptual: an ordered pair reads (x, y). Here that is (hours, liters). The first number tells how far ACROSS. The second tells how far UP.
map.Procedural: walk along the hours axis to: Procedural: go along the hours axis to the logged hour, then go straight up to the logged liters. Tap the point where those two lines meet.
map.A hatch under the irrigation deck. Insid: A hatch under the irrigation deck. Inside: the dome's first climate controller. Older than the glass.
map.Found our villain. No mastermind — just: Found our villain. No mastermind, just a rusty controller. Look at the wiring.
map.It's been reading temperature as the INP: It has been reading temperature as the INPUT and fan time as the OUTPUT. It mixed up cause and effect.
map.Confirmed. It swapped the independent an: Confirmed. It swapped the independent and dependent variables. For years the dome has been commanding the thermometer and obeying the fans. Sad. Almost poetic.
map.Final quest chain: reseed the wilted row: Final quest: reseed the wilted rows while we rewire. The seed drone drops 9 pods every minute it flies. Rule: d = 9t.
map.The drone's equation: d = 9t, where t =: The drone's equation: d = 9t, where t = minutes flying (independent) and d = seed pods dropped (dependent).
map.Fly the drone by the rule, reader. The w: Fly the drone by the rule, reader. The wilted rows are counting on you.
map.The seed drone obeys d = 9t (t = minutes: The seed drone follows d = 9t (t = minutes flying → d = seed pods dropped). Use the rule both ways to reseed the wilted rows.
map.Conceptual: an equation is a two-way mac: Conceptual: an equation is a two-way machine. Put in a time t and it finds the pods d. If you already know d, run the machine backward to find t.
map.Procedural: forward — substitute the t-v: Procedural: forward: substitute the t-value and multiply by 9. Backward: ask '9 times WHAT minutes gives that many pods?' Division undoes the multiplication.
map.The controller hatch, 4:51 AM. Sunrise i: The controller hatch, 4:51 AM. Sunrise in nine minutes. Three wire locks left.
map.Three locks stand between this dome and: Three locks stand between this dome and sunrise. Each one is a relationship the controller must learn again.
map.Temperature recovery, the water budget,: Temperature recovery, the water budget, and one last wiring question. Reader, hands on.
map.Cross these wires right, and the dome wa: Cross these wires right, and the dome wakes up with the sun.
map.Boss Gate: substitute, compute, compare: Boss Gate: substitute, compute, compare. And show you know which variable depends on which.
map.Sunrise is coming. Three wire locks — ea: Sunrise is coming. Three wire locks, each a relationship the controller must learn again. Substitute, compute, compare... and tag the variables right this time.
map.Recovery rule y = x + 15 (y = temp in °F: Recovery rule y = x + 15 (y = temp in °F, x = hours since reset). At x = 20 hours, y =
map.Final rewiring — in w = 6h, which is the: Final rewiring: in w = 6h, which is the INDEPENDENT variable?
map.Conceptual: every lock is one rule relat: Conceptual: every lock is one rule linking two variables. Substitute the value you KNOW. The rule finds the one you don't. And remember the controller's old mistake: be sure which variable is the answer.
map.Procedural: Lock 1 — replace x with the: Procedural: Lock 1: replace x with the hours, then add. Lock 2: multiply the hours by 6, then compare your answer with the 60-liter capacity. Lock 3: the independent variable is the INPUT, the quantity you choose freely. The rule finds the other one from it.
map.Rows up! Mist clearing! Temperature righ: Rows up! Mist clearing! The temperature is right where the rule said it would be.
map.The controller finally asks the right qu: The controller finally asks the right question: what depends on what.
map.Achievement unlocked: harvest saved. Rol: Achievement unlocked: harvest saved. Roll credits?
map.…Crew. The Pattern Engine is waking bene: ...Crew. The Pattern Engine is waking beneath the city. Every district is glowing, and five silhouettes stand over its heart. Four of us. And you. Not a bent pattern. A beginning.
map.Crew captain. Keeps the notebook, asks t: Crew captain. Keeps the notebook and asks the next question. This volume: co-led the dome rescue and called the final rewiring.
map.Evidence officer. Tests every rule on ev: Evidence officer. Tests every rule on every row. This volume: read the table that showed the dome's water rule.
map.Builder and fixer. Keeps the sensors hon: Builder and fixer. Keeps the sensors honest. This volume: rewired a controller older than she is.
Pattern hunter. Co-led the dome rescue. This volume: flew the seed drone by its own equation.
map.Fragment of Ada Vex's Pattern Engine. Se: A piece of Ada Vex's Pattern Engine. Senses bent patterns but cannot compute. That's your job.
map.Independent variable.The quantity you ch: Independent variable.The quantity you change on purpose, the cause. The fans' running time.
map.Dependent variable.The quantity that res: Dependent variable.The quantity that responds, the effect. The dome's temperature.
map.Graph.A picture of the relationship. Rea: Graph.A picture of the relationship. Read left to right: a falling line = going down, a flat line = holding steady.
map.Table & equation.A table lists matching: Table & equation.A table lists matching x–y pairs. An equation like y = 4x is the rule behind them. A true rule works for every row.
map.Coordinate pair.(x, y) marks one moment:: Coordinate pair.(x, y) marks one moment: independent value first, dependent value second. (5, 20) is not (20, 5).
map.completed Volume 9: Cause & Effect and p: completed Volume 9: Cause & Effect and showed skill with independent and dependent variables, graphs of relationships, tables, equations, and coordinate pairs.
map.Different scenario: 'The more minutes a: A different scenario: 'The more minutes a candle burns, the shorter it gets.'
map.Burn time is the quantity being allowed: Burn time is the quantity you let change on purpose. It is the independent variable (the cause).
map.The candle's height responds to that tim: The candle's height responds to that time. It is the dependent variable (the effect).
map.In 'the more laps you swim, the more tir: In 'the more laps you swim, the more tired you feel', which is the dependent variable: laps or tired?
map.Flat piece = no change — the tap is off;: Flat piece = no change. The tap is off, so the level holds. Story: 'it rises, then stays put.'
map.On a graph, a line that stays flat the w: On a graph, a line that stays flat the whole time shows a quantity that is... (write: changing or constant)
map.Watch out: 'add 2' also fits the first r: Watch out: 'add 2' also fits the first row (1+2=3), but row two breaks it (2+2=4, not 6). One lucky row proves nothing.
map.Different pump, rule y = 2x: the reading: A different pump, rule y = 2x: the reading 'after 3 hours, 6 liters' becomes the pair (3, 6).
map.Across to 3 on the hours axis, up to 6 o: Across to 3 on the hours axis, up to 6 on the liters axis. That's the point.
map.(6, 3) sits somewhere else entirely: 6 h: (6, 3) is somewhere else: 6 hours, 3 liters. Swapping the order changes the story.
map.With rule y = 2x, which number comes FIR: With rule y = 2x, which number comes FIRST in the pair for 4 hours: 4 or 8?
map.Backward: if p = 35, ask 5 × what = 35 →: Backward: if p = 35, ask 5 × what = 35 → n = 7 minutes.
map.Its water rule m = 4t: at t = 7, m = 4 ×: Its water rule m = 4t: at t = 7, m = 4 × 7 = 28 liters. Tank capacity 30 → 28 ≤ 30, so it fits.
map.In m = 4t, t is the value you choose and: In m = 4t, t is the value you choose and m is found FROM it. So t is the independent variable, and m is the dependent one.
map.Pick one tag in EACH group — a cause and: Pick one tag in EACH group: a cause and an effect.
map.Fan time is the cause you control; the t: Fan time is the cause you control. The temperature answers it. Tagged and logged!
map.Swapped! That's the old controller's exa: Swapped! That is the old controller's exact mistake. The temperature does not make the fans run.
map.The fans' color never changes and change: The fans' color never changes and changes nothing. It isn't a variable in this story.
map.The crops care about the result, but the: The crops care about the result, but they aren't one of the two changing quantities in the sentence.
map.One tag is off. Ask: which quantity do w: One tag is off. Ask: which quantity do we SET, and which one REACTS?
map.Falling line, then flat line — cooling,: Falling line, then flat line: cooling, then holding. You read the dome's story well.
map.Read left to right, like a sentence — on: Read left to right, like a sentence. On this graph the FALL comes first, then the flat part.
map.Rising first would slant UP at the start: Rising first would slant UP at the start. But this line starts by falling, and it never climbs back.
map.Falling then rising would make a V shape: Falling then rising would make a V shape. After the fall, this line stays flat.
map.Careful — y = x + 3 works for (1, 4) onl: Careful: y = x + 3 works for (1, 4) only. Test EVERY row: is 2 + 3 = 8? Keep the rule that works for all four.
map.y = 4 + x fails the very first row: 4 +: y = 4 + x fails the very first row: 4 + 1 = 5, but the table says 4.
map.y = x ÷ 4 would make the liters tiny — b: y = x ÷ 4 would make the liters tiny. But in this table the liters are BIGGER than the hours.
map.The missing cell breaks the pattern the: The missing cell breaks the pattern of the first three rows. Check it again before the rule.
map.Cell's right — now pick the equation tha: The cell is right. Now pick the equation that matches every row.
map.y = 4x — four liters every hour, twenty: y = 4x: four liters every hour, twenty at five. The dome drinks on a schedule.
map.(5, 20) — five hours across, twenty lite: (5, 20): five hours across, twenty liters up. The pump's exact last words.
map.Order matters: (hours, liters). That poi: Order matters: (hours, liters). That point says twenty HOURS and only five liters. That is the swapped story.
map.Twenty liters, yes — but slide across: t: Twenty liters, yes. But slide across: the log said FIVE hours, and that point sits at four.
map.Five hours, yes — but climb higher: does: Five hours, yes. But climb higher: does fifteen liters match the reading?
map.You multiplied again — going from d back: You multiplied again. Going from d back to t runs the rule in REVERSE.
map.Pods out on leg one, three minutes back: Pods out on leg one, three minutes back on leg two. The rule works both ways. Rows reseeded!
map.Lock 1 holds. x + 15 says ADD 15 — you m: Lock 1 holds. x + 15 says ADD 15. You multiplied.
map.Lock 3 holds. w is the OUTPUT the rule c: Lock 3 holds. w is the OUTPUT the rule finds. That makes it the dependent one. Which quantity do you get to SET?
map.Lock 3 holds. The 6 is a constant — it n: Lock 3 holds. The 6 is a constant. It never changes, so it can't be a variable at all.
map.Lock 3 holds. Both vary, but only ONE is: Lock 3 holds. Both change, but only ONE is freely chosen. The other is found from it.
map.Lock 3 needs an answer — which variable: Lock 3 needs an answer: which variable is the input you control?
map.ALL LOCKS OPEN. Cause back in command, e: ALL LOCKS OPEN. Cause is back in command, effect answers on cue. The controller hums, the mist lifts, and sunrise lands on glowing rows. CAUSE & EFFECT!
